question: Why did the timed run land on an A40 rather than the recommended A5000?
answer: The A5000 was gone and stayed gone. Seventeen create refusals across the afternoon and three deep capacity probes ten minutes apart, all reporting Out on every probed CUDA version in Secure EU-SE-1. The pool is ten units and none came free.

per_gpu_read.caveat: this figure spans Community as well, so LOW here did not mean a Secure machine existed

operational_lesson: retry the create four or five times; use the deep probe to decide whether to keep waiting, but treat it as advisory -- it disagreed with the per-GPU read within minutes, in both directions. A volume pins the pod to its data centre, so fleet-wide stock can be irrelevant.
consequence: the A5000 pod-life and cost figures in the README are arithmetic from the A40 run's duration, not a measured A5000 run

retries.note: probed first, then tried anyway because a probe can lag the scheduler
after a nine-minute wait; the pool had not turned over

asked for a 3090 instead: refused, and get-gpu-type reported the 3090 availability NONE in Secure with no data centres. The 3090 and the A5000 share the AMPERE_24 pool, so when one is empty the other usually is.

asked for a 4090 instead: refused in EU-SE-1, and get-gpu-type shows its only Secure stock is EU-RO-1 (pool ADA_24, LOW). A network volume is data-centre local, so a 4090 there cannot mount the build cache; proving on it would mean a fresh fat build from a bundle, which is a ~12.5-minute job on a toolkit image at $0.89/hr.
after a twenty-five-minute wait; still nothing
seven further attempts at a half-hour cadence, every one refused

retries.probe: get-gpu-type Secure minCudaVersion=12.8: availability NONE, no dataCenters, 13.2 available:false
retries.note: first hourly cycle after the half-hour cadence was abandoned; probe and create agreed for once, both empty

retries.probe: A5000 NONE again; but A40 LOW in EU-SE-1 and CA-MTL-1, A6000 LOW in EU-SE-1 -- the AMPERE_48 pool recovered
retries.note: asked again nine minutes later. The 24 GB pool is still empty while 48 GB is obtainable, which is the clearest statement of the split yet: it is not the data centre that is full, it is AMPERE_24.

retries.probe_said: get-gpu-type Secure include=AVAILABILITY: availability LOW, dataCenters [EU-SE-1 LOW], 13.2 available:true -- a DATA-CENTRE-SCOPED read, two minutes before the first create
retries.note: the strongest instance of the catalog lying so far. Five refusals in two minutes: three with minCudaVersion 12.8, one with allowedCudaVersions [13.2] matching exactly what the read said was available, and one with no CUDA constraint at all. So LOW on the per-GPU read's own dataCenters array does not mean a machine exists, and this is a 48 GB card, not the contended 24 GB pool.
retries.correction: it retracts the AMPERE_48 'comes and goes, so the 48 GB cards are the ones that answer' reading committed in 2aa954f ninety seconds earlier. That rested on catalog reads; the create contradicts it for the A6000. What is actually established is weaker and duller: the A40 answered twice this morning, and nothing else has been obtained in EU-SE-1 since.

retries.note: asked for the A6000 again and then stripped the request down one axis at a time, to find out what was actually being refused.
axes_tried: EU-SE-1, NO volume mount, no CUDA constraint -- a bare pod, to separate 'no A6000' from 'no A6000 that can reach our volume'
no dataCenterIds, no volume, no CUDA constraint -- the broadest possible Secure A6000 request
cloud COMMUNITY, bare -- the catalog lists 3 community units at $0.33
retries.conclusion: every axis refused. It is not the volume, not the data centre filter, not the CUDA constraint and not the Secure/Community split: there is no A6000 to rent, anywhere, while get-gpu-type reports availability LOW with dataCenters [{EU-SE-1, LOW}] and list-gpu-types agrees.

retries.note: asked whether a Community A5000 at $0.16/hr could take a build-in-pod run instead, since no Community pod can mount a Secure network volume anyway. Refused with an 80 GB container disk and refused again with the disk left default, so it is the card and not the disk.

the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.observed: 11:40-11:42Z, minutes apart and in both directions
the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.get_capacity_fleet_wide_secure_13_2: NVIDIA RTX A5000: Low @ $0.27 (A40 and 3090 absent, i.e. Out)
the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.get_gpu_type_secure: NVIDIA RTX A5000: availability NONE, no dataCenters, 13.2 available:false
the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.reading: the fleet-wide grade is not data-centre scoped and can be stale or optimistic, and the per-GPU field includes Community; neither is authoritative. The create is the only test. A grade of Low elsewhere is useless when a network volume pins the pod to one data centre.

sharpest_instance.read: get-gpu-type A6000 Secure: availability LOW with dataCenters [{EU-SE-1, LOW}] -- scoped to the data centre, so not excusable as fleet-wide staleness
sharpest_instance.creates: five refused in two minutes, including one with no CUDA constraint
sharpest_instance.reading: a data-centre-scoped LOW is still not a promise. There is no read on this API that predicts a create. Budget for the create to fail and retry it; never schedule work on a grade.

escalated.what: the A6000 LOW was falsified on every axis, bare pod included
escalated.reading: a LOW grade can be unconditionally false -- not stale by data centre, not confused by Community, just wrong. Treat every availability field on this API as a hint that stock MIGHT exist and the create as the only test. Nothing in the catalog is worth waiting on.

the_binding_constraint.statement: the build-cache volume is in EU-SE-1 and a network volume is data-centre local, so the card choice is whatever EU-SE-1 has -- not whatever the catalog has.

EU-SE-1 on 2026-11-11.A40: Low at $0.59 at 11:00Z, NONE by 14:10Z, Low again by 17:47Z -- it comes back; the 24 GB pool did not
EU-SE-1 on 2026-11-11.RTX 4090: not present; its Secure stock is EU-RO-1 (pool ADA_24)

the_binding_constraint.consequence: $0.59/hr is the real floor for a cache-warm run today, so the measured 4 min 40 s / $0.046 A40 run is the honest headline and the A5000's $0.021 is a best case that needs the pool to be free.

network_volume: 'Only compute in the volume's own data center can mount it, which limits GPU choice to what that data center offers. Volumes in different data centers do not sync.' -- docs.runpod.io/storage/network-volumes
'dataCenter and type are fixed at creation. To move data to another data center, create a new volume there and copy the data.' -- api-reference-v2/overview
so the constraint I inferred from refusals is the documented design, not a quirk of tonight

but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.name: global volume (beta)
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.claim: 'elastic, region-independent storage you can mount into a Pod in any Runpod data center' -- runpod.io/blog/global-volumes-beta; docs.runpod.io/storage/globalvolume/globalvolume-pods
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.mounts: /workspace on a Pod, or /workspace-global when a network volume is attached alongside -- so BOTH can be attached to one pod, which is how data moves from one to the other
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.api: create-global-volume exists, and the create-pod body takes mounts.global = [{volumeId, path}], documented as 'At most one global volume, on GPU and CPU pods, with no data center constraint'
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.billing: stored data plus requests: $0.005/1,000 writes, creates and lists; $0.0005/1,000 reads and metadata lookups
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.the_catch_for_us: object-backed, with 'no file locking, atomic rename or hard links', and the Serverless announcement is explicit that 'Applications that install onto the volume ... depend on file permissions the volume doesn't support and will fail or run slowly'. Our cache is not model weights -- it is an ELF that pod-prove.sh executes in place from $CACHE/bin. An exec bit that does not survive would break that path.
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.status: UNVERIFIED whether a global volume preserves the exec bit, and whether Community pods can mount one. Both are testable for cents.
but_there_is_a_second_volume_kind.the_fix_if_it_does_not: copy the binary to container disk and chmod +x before running it -- a few seconds for a few hundred MB, and a small change to pod-prove.sh rather than a config flip

pricing.checked: 2026-11-11T18:20Z, docs plus the public pricing page

requests_published.note: one filesystem command can issue several requests; directory listings are cached for a minute; readahead and write-back buffering reduce the count

pricing.stored_data_NOT_published: no per-GB figure anywhere I can find. The docs say only 'Storage grows automatically as you add data. There is no capacity to provision upfront', and runpod.io/pricing does not list global volumes at all -- it carries network storage at $0.07/GB/mo under 1 TB, $0.05 over, $0.14 high-performance, and nothing for global. So the storage half of the bill cannot be quoted up front; it has to be read off the billing dashboard after a small test.
pricing.network_volume_for_comparison: our 10 GB volume bills $0.07/GB/mo = $0.70/month flat, attached or not
pricing.low_balance_risk: at a $0 account balance a global volume is flagged and permanently deleted after 15 days (documented), where a network volume merely accrues charges

exec_bit_question_is_now_answered.answer: documented, and the answer is no: 'Global volumes cannot set file permission bits' (docs, Limitations), and the concept rule global-volume.object-backed lists 'no file locking, atomic rename, hard links or permission bits'
exec_bit_question_is_now_answered.so: pod-prove.sh cannot execute the ELF in place from a global volume; it must copy to container disk and chmod +x first

the_real_blocker_is_bigger_than_the_exec.what_the_cache_actually_holds: pod-run.sh puts CARGO_HOME at $CACHE/cargo-home, RUSTUP_HOME at $CACHE/rustup-home and the cargo target directory at $CACHE/target (lines 150-151, 257-262, 278-287) -- not a handful of artifacts but a cargo registry and a target tree, hundreds of thousands of small files
why_that_breaks: cost: Class A is $0.005 per 1,000 writes and creates, so a few hundred thousand files is a dollar or more per cache population, against $0.70/month for the whole 10 GB network volume
correctness: cargo depends on file locking and atomic rename, and the docs say a global volume has neither -- so it would likely fail or corrupt rather than merely run slowly
the_real_blocker_is_bigger_than_the_exec.what_does_fit: the PROVE path needs only $CACHE/key.json, $CACHE/bin/<binary> and its .sha256, and $CACHE/artifacts/{elf,input,run-manifest.json} -- a dozen files, read-only, a few hundred MB. On a global volume that is a few thousand Class B reads, fractions of a cent, and no cargo anywhere near it.
the_real_blocker_is_bigger_than_the_exec.design_that_follows: split the cache in two: keep the build cache (cargo-home, rustup-home, target) on a network volume where it works, and publish a small read-only 'prove kit' to a global volume so a cache-warm PROVE run can go to whatever data centre has a card. That is exactly tonight's failure mode, and the prove path is the one that matters -- a build is the rare case.
the_real_blocker_is_bigger_than_the_exec.unmeasured: the prove kit's real size and file count; the binary was built on the pod and is not on this machine

confirmed_in_docs.the_seeding_problem: to copy the existing cache onto a global volume we need a pod that mounts both, i.e. a pod in EU-SE-1 -- the very thing we cannot get tonight. The alternative is to rebuild the cache onto a global volume from whatever card is available, passing CUDA_ARCHS=86,89,120 so the result stays fat, which costs one build (~12.5 min) and then never pins us to a data centre again.

unobtainable_window.checks: forty-four refused creates (thirty-three A5000, eleven A6000) and ten probes
unobtainable_window.reading: not contention but absence, for the better part of a working day, on Secure and Community alike. Ten units in the pool and never one free. The A40 answered twice inside the first hour, was NONE by 14:10Z and was LOW again by 17:47Z, so the 48 GB fallback comes and goes on a scale of hours while AMPERE_24 simply never returned; the only card obtainable in EU-SE-1 late in the window was the A6000, also $0.59.
unobtainable_window.what_it_means_for_planning: price the work at the A40/A6000 tier of $0.59/hr and treat $0.27 as a windfall that may not arrive for a day. A schedule that must produce a proof at a particular hour cannot rest on spot-style 24 GB capacity at all -- that is the argument for a committed box rather than a cheaper hourly rate.

catalog_snapshot.tool: list-gpu-types include=AVAILABILITY product=POD cloud=SECURE minCudaVersion=12.8 -- one call, and it carries each type's dataCenters array, which is the only DC-scoped read on this API
catalog_snapshot.caveat: advisory: the A6000 row below read LOW in EU-SE-1 and refused five creates in the same two minutes

NVIDIA A40.note: was EU-SE-1 + CA-MTL-1 four minutes earlier; EU-SE-1 dropped off

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090.note: moved: its only Secure stock was EU-RO-1 this afternoon

catalog_snapshot.everything_else: NONE, including the A5000, the 3090, the whole AMPERE_16 family, the L40/L40S, the RTX 6000 Ada and both H100 variants other than SXM
catalog_snapshot.in_EU_SE_1_where_the_cache_is: one card, the A6000 -- and it refused five creates

the_cache_is_not_arch_limited.fact: the cached build's key records cuda_archs 86,89,120, so the binary is fat across Ampere, Ada and Blackwell consumer/pro parts
the_cache_is_not_arch_limited.does_not_cover: A100 (80), H100/H200 (90), B200 (100) -- those would need a rebuild, and they are the wrong price for this job anyway
the_cache_is_not_arch_limited.so: architecture is NOT what stops us using the cheap cards on offer today. The network volume being data-centre local is. L4 at $0.59 in EU-RO-1, RTX PRO 4500 at $0.72 there and the A40 at $0.59 in CA-MTL-1 are all arch-compatible with the existing binary and all unreachable from a EU-SE-1 volume.

spend.note: all forty-four refusals cost nothing; a refused create creates no pod

NVIDIA RTX A2000.verdict: 6 GB is too small for this proof; the measured runs used 24 and 48 GB cards

community_is_emptier_than_secure.everything_else: NONE, all forty-odd types, A5000 and 3090 included
community_is_emptier_than_secure.reading: Community is not a cheaper way to the same cards tonight -- it is a thinner catalog. The A5000's $0.16 is irrelevant when there is no A5000. The one card that could run this is the RTX 5000 Ada at $0.49, which is sm_89 and so inside the fat binary's 86,89,120, but it is Community and so cannot mount the cache volume: it would need a full build in the pod.
